tests.title: Toolset has exactly the five documented fields in order
given: the root package agentkit
tests.when: reflect.TypeOf(agentkit.Toolset{}) is inspected
then: fields are Tools []core.Tool, Policy core.ToolPolicy, Guard core.BeforeToolCall, After core.AfterToolCall, Events func(core.Event), in that order
there are no other fields
tests.pseudocode: t = TypeOf(Toolset{}); assert names(t) == [Tools,Policy,Guard,After,Events]; assert type(Events) == func(core.Event)

tests.title: Config has exactly twelve fields and none of the four moved tool fields
given: the root package agentkit
tests.when: reflect.TypeOf(agentkit.Config{}) is inspected
then: field names in order are Client, Provider, Model, Effort, System, Prefix, Toolset, MaxTurns, MaxCostUSD, Timeout, Prune, MaxTokens
Tools, Policy, Guard and After are absent
the Toolset field has type agentkit.Toolset
tests.pseudocode: assert names(TypeOf(Config{})) == [12 names]; assert no field named Tools|Policy|Guard|After

tests.title: A zero Toolset yields an agent with no tools and no tool definitions in the first request
given: a scripted provider that records requests and answers with a final text message
a valid model
tests.when: New(Config{Provider, Model}) is called and a.Run(ctx, "hi") is executed
then: New returns a non-nil agent and nil error
a.Runner().Tools() has length 0
the first recorded request carries zero tool definitions
tests.pseudocode: a,err = New(Config{Provider:p, Model:m}); assert err==nil; assert len(a.Runner().Tools())==0; a.Run(ctx,"hi"); assert len(p.requests[0].Tools)==0

tests.title: NewRunner checks in today's order and returns the first failure; a valid set returns a runner
given: a toolset whose first tool has neither Handler nor Execute and which also exposes an unguarded shell tool
a toolset whose policy-resolved set contains a tool with both Handler and Execute
a valid toolset with a guard
tests.when: NewRunner is called on each
then: the first returns the neither-Handler-nor-Execute error, not the ErrUnguardedExecute error
the second returns the sets-both error from the resolved-set check
the valid one returns a non-nil runner and nil error
each failure returns a nil *Runner
tests.pseudocode: r,err = NewRunner(ts1); assert r==nil && contains(err,'has neither Handler nor Execute'); ...

tests.title: NewRunner refuses a tool with neither or both of Handler and Execute with the exact texts
given: tool "t" with no Handler and no Execute
tool "u" with both Handler and Execute
tests.when: NewRunner is called with each, directly and via a policy-resolved wrapper
then: error text equals `agentkit: tool "t" has neither Handler nor Execute`
error text equals `agentkit: tool "u" sets both Handler and Execute; exactly one`
the returned *Runner is nil
tests.pseudocode: r,err = NewRunner(Toolset{Tools:[t]}); assert r==nil; assert err.Error()==want

tests.title: NewRunner refuses reachable-tool cycles and wrappers reaching terminating tools
given: tools a -> b -> a by ReachableTools names
a wrapper "codemode" reaching a tool marked Terminating
tests.when: NewRunner is called with each toolset
then: cycle error text is `agentkit: reachable tools cycle detected: a -> b -> a`
terminating error text is `agentkit: terminating tool "x" cannot be reached through wrapper "codemode"`
runner is nil in both cases
tests.pseudocode: r,err = NewRunner(cyclicPair()); assert r==nil; assert err.Error()=='agentkit: reachable tools cycle detected: a -> b -> a'

tests.title: NewRunner refuses a reachable shell tool with a nil Guard and names Toolset.Guard
given: a direct shell tool "run_command" and a wrapper reaching a shell tool, each with nil Guard
tests.when: NewRunner is called with each
then: errors.Is(err, core.ErrUnguardedExecute) is true
text contains `Toolset.Guard is nil` and does not contain `Config.Guard`
text ends with ` (tool "run_command")` for the direct case and ` (wrapper "…" reached shell tool "…")` for the wrapper case
runner is nil
tests.pseudocode: r,err = NewRunner(Toolset{Tools:[shell]}); assert errors.Is(err, ErrUnguardedExecute); assert HasSuffix(err.Error(), ' (tool "run_command")')

tests.title: NewRunner and New report identical errors for any toolset
given: a stub provider and model so New passes its client and model checks
tests.when: for any generated Toolset mixing valid tools, tools with missing or doubled Handler/Execute, cycles, terminating tools behind wrappers, shell tools, nil or non-nil Guard, and policies
then: NewRunner(ts) returns an error exactly when New(Config{Provider, Model, Toolset: ts}) does
when both fail the error texts are identical; when both succeed both errors are nil
tests.pseudocode: for ts in gen(): _,e1 = NewRunner(ts); _,e2 = New(Config{...,Toolset:ts}); assert (e1==nil)==(e2==nil); if e1 != nil: assert e1.Error()==e2.Error()

tests.title: Mutating the caller's Tools slice after NewRunner does not change the runner
given: a Tools slice with tools alpha and beta
tests.when: NewRunner copies it, then the caller overwrites element 0 and appends gamma
then: r.Tools() names are still alpha, beta
tests.pseudocode: r = NewRunner(Toolset{Tools:s}); s[0]=other; s=append(s,gamma); assert names(r.Tools())==[alpha,beta]

tests.title: A runner is safe for concurrent Call, Batch, Tools and Reachable under the race detector
given: a runner over echo tools and a code-mode-like wrapper, with Guard, After and Events set to concurrency-safe functions

then: no data race is reported
every Call and Batch returns a result of the expected shape
tests.pseudocode: wg; for i in 0..16: go func(){ r.Call(...); r.Batch(...); r.Tools(); r.Reachable() }

tests.title: Runner.Tools returns the policy-resolved set in policy order as a fresh slice

then: names and order equal ts.Policy.Resolve(ts.Tools)
the second result is unaffected by the overwrite
tests.pseudocode: a = r.Tools(); a[0]=core.Tool{}; b = r.Tools(); assert names(b)==names(policy.Resolve(tools))

tests.title: Runner.Reachable and Agent.ReachableTools equal core.ReachableTools over the resolved set

tests.title: *Agent exports exactly Run, Stream, Messages, Usage, ReachableTools and Runner

tests.title: Runner.Call runs a batch of one with a generated call_ id and returns a result

tests.title: Empty or whitespace input is treated as {}

tests.title: An unknown tool name gives unknown_tool with the run's text and runs neither guard nor handler

tests.title: Non-object input, failed validation and unencodable guard arguments give invalid_arguments

a Guard that returns Arguments containing a channel value for another call

tests.title: A guard block gives blocked_by_policy with the reason, default reason, and the decision's Terminate

tests.title: A handler panic gives panic and a Handler error gives handler_error; Call returns normally

a tool whose Handler returns an error

then: the first has OK false and code panic
the second has OK false and code handler_error
Call neither panics nor returns a Go error

tests.title: A done context gives aborted without starting the handler

tests.title: Guard sees the documented context for a Call

tests.title: Batch emits start events in call order and runs all Guards before any handler

tests.title: Handlers overlap when concurrent, never overlap with a Sequential tool, and After never overlaps

then: the two blocking handlers overlap in time
with a Sequential tool present handlers never overlap and run in call order
no two After invocations of one batch overlap

tests.title: Each result's Terminate is the call's final vote

tests.title: A wrapper's nested call gets a nested_ id, parent fields in Guard and After, parent events and no result event

tests.title: The exported-API golden records Toolset, NewRunner, Runner and the new Config
given: internal/policy/testdata/exported-api.golden regenerated and committed
tests.when: TS-13-67 runs without AGENTKIT_UPDATE_API_GOLDEN set
then: it passes
the golden mentions Toolset with five fields, NewRunner, Runner with Call, Batch, Tools and Reachable, Agent.Runner and the twelve-field Config
tests.pseudocode: go test ./internal/policy -run TS-13-67; assert golden contains the declarations

tests.title: The core and root-module line budgets still hold
given: the repository after the change
tests.when: TS-12-14 runs
then: core is at or under 1,600 lines of code
the root module is at or under 20,000
tests.pseudocode: go test ./core -run TS-12-14

tests.title: An embedder runs code mode through a runner with no agent
given: a temp workspace with a file
a code_mode tool over tools.For, a Guard and an Events sink
tests.when: NewRunner(Toolset{Tools, Guard, Events}) is built and r.Call(ctx, "code_mode", script) runs a script calling read_file
then: NewRunner returns a runner
the result is OK with the file content
Events holds nested start and end events for read_file with ParentToolUseID equal to the code_mode call id
Events holds the code_mode end and result events

tests.title: An agent run executes a turn's two tool calls through its runner
given: a scripted provider returning an assistant message with two tool calls then a final answer
tests.when: agentkit.New(Config{Provider, Model, Toolset}) and a.Run(ctx, prompt) execute
then: the first request's tool definitions equal Runner.Tools()
handlers ran for both calls, start, end and result events reached the run's stream
the transcript holds two ToolResultMessages and the final assistant answer

tests.title: A misconfigured toolset is refused before any request
given: a recording provider and a toolset exposing run_command with a nil Toolset.Guard
tests.when: agentkit.New is called
then: it returns a nil agent and an error wrapping core.ErrUnguardedExecute naming Toolset.Guard
the provider received no request

tests.title: The harness example runs offline through a runner and prints its success line
given: the harness example in offline mode with its scripted provider and fake proxies
tests.when: the program is run
then: output contains `Harness example completed successfully`
the process exits 0
call and blocked counts are printed from the hooks
MCP-served tool calls and the final git status ran through Runner.Call
